Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: 6–7 day history of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic aching pain, and pink-tinged urine; baseline IBS.  
- Relevant family medical history: No known kidney or bladder disease; other family history not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented; Mebeverine for IBS – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; unprotected intercourse ~1 week ago; uses combined OCP; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; denies abnormal vaginal discharge.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Eating and drinking “OK”; physical activity not discussed.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Social alcohol use; non-smoker; single cannabis use 1.5 weeks ago.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives in university halls with flat-mate; family nearby and supportive; first-year English student.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.

- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded (not yet due by guidelines).  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.  
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Young woman with classic lower urinary tract symptoms (dysuria, frequency, suprapubic discomfort, micro-hematuria) and no systemic or flank features. Past medical history significant for IBS; sexually active with recent unprotected intercourse.

Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial UTI).

Differential diagnoses (from DDx and consistent with transcript):  
• Acute uncomplicated cystitis – high likelihood given symptom triad, absence of systemic signs.  
• Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – moderate likelihood; sexual risk factors and overlapping symptoms but no discharge or pelvic pain reported.  

Management priorities: Obtain mid-stream urine (MSU) for dipstick/microscopy, culture & sensitivity; commence empiric oral antibiotic (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin 3-day course) pending culture; advise hydration and simple analgesia; counsel on red-flag symptoms; arrange review if no improvement.

Management Plan

- Prescription: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin 3-day course (specific agent not confirmed).  
- Investigation: Provide container and instructions for MSU; sample to be dropped at clinic for dipstick and culture.  
- Symptom control: Encourage ↑ oral fluids; paracetamol for pain.  
- Safety-netting: Seek medical care if fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or worsening symptoms; routine follow-up next week if no improvement.  
- Education: Discussed low likelihood of cannabis contributing; advised against future use; reinforced safe sex and potential need for STI testing (not arranged during call).  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: classic dysuria, frequency, suprapubic pain, mild hematuria, no systemic features.  
2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – Moderate likelihood: recent unprotected sex, dysuria overlaps; absence of discharge reduces likelihood.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

• Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse, temperature), BMI/waist, immunisation review, mental health screening, hearing/vision/oral/ear examination, urinalysis result, STI screen, alcohol intake quantification.  
• Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
